newsitem.title: JAPAN: IAE to aim for $2 bln 1996 aircraft engine orders.
newsitem.headline: IAE to aim for $2 bln 1996 aircraft engine orders.

text.p: International Aero Engines (IAE), a consortium which includes Japanese companies, said on Wednesday that it plans to win a total $2 billion worth of aircraft engine orders by the end of December.
IAE president Barry Eccleston told a news conference in Tokyo that the group has already received aircraft engine orders worth more than $1.6 billion so far this year.

IAE expects orders for 24 more aircraft engines in the remaining months of 1996, he said. That would bring the total for this year to about $1.8 billion, but the consortium hopes to receive additional orders and achieve its target, he said.

The Japanese members of the consortium are Kawasaki Heavy Industries Ltd, Ishikawajima-Harima Heavy Industries Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries. The other companies are Rolls-Royce Plc, United Technologies Corp's unit Pratt & Whitney, and Daimler-Benz AG's unit MTU.
